title: Choose Pesoprint's visual world: retro and steampunk
question: Re-rolled with your steer. The roll assigned The Ironmonger's Window. Keep it, take my pick, or re-roll again. None of the dealt catalogue worlds beat it, so they appear as compact rows.

options.label: The Ironmonger's Window
options.lineage: Victorian ironmongers' and engineers' supply shops: reverse-gilded glass fascias, enamel signs, brass fittings, window displays
options.thesis: Pesoprint as a workshop shopfront: the objects sit in the window, and gold leaf on black glass names the shop.
options.viewport: A gilded glass fascia across the top, then a three-bay shop window (Free, Files, Printed to order), each bay a shelf of real objects with brass price tickets, and search set on a brass door plate.
options.risk: Can slide into steampunk costume (gears everywhere, sepia). Colours must stay true, and gold-leaf type only works at display sizes.

raised.raise: Test strip: the colour picker shows the model in every available colour as one banded strip before you commit.
No gradients or soft shadows. Depth in the window comes only from overlapping flat planes: glass, shelf, card, object.
One specimen scale: the gilded face is used at three fixed sizes (fascia, window card, ticket), never mixed with a second display face.
Show-cards annotate: small hand-lettered cards point at real facts on each object (size, material, print time).
One idea per bay: each section below the window is a single full-width bay with one job.
Each department (Free, Files, Print service) keeps its own enamel sign colour everywhere on the site.

options.label: The Pattern Shop
options.lineage: foundry pattern shops, where wooden master patterns were painted in a colour code before casting
options.thesis: Every model is a master pattern, the original you make copies from.
options.viewport: One large painted master pattern on a sand-grey bench, with a stencilled pattern number and the three ways to get it as hanging stencilled tags.
options.risk: Less familiar than it looks: pattern-making is obscure outside engineering circles, and the shop floor can read dusty if the paint colours are timid.

options.label: Cut-paper Titles
options.thesis: The shop told in flat cut-paper cards on bold colour fields.
options.case: Retro but not steampunk, and silhouettes hide the objects' real colours.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Orders move through stations like prints through baths.
options.viewport: Stations from choose to ship under amber light.
options.case: The amber wash hides filament colour, which is the product.
options.kept: Test strips: preview every colour before committing.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Models built up layer by layer, like prints.
options.case: Nice link to layer-by-layer printing, but folk craft rather than retro engineering.
options.kept: Depth only from overlapping flat planes.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: A towering pixel headline over dense columns.
options.case: The wrong era for the steer, and type-led rather than object-led.
options.kept: One display face at a strict size scale.

options.label: Hand-drawn Explainer
options.thesis: A friend sketching how printing works.
options.case: Friendly but not retro, and it uses the cream-paper default.
options.kept: Annotating cards that point at real facts.

options.label: Sleeping City
options.thesis: A city folding into a quilt.
options.case: No link to the product or the steer.
options.kept: Each department keeps its own colour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A 3D-model site like the big repositories, done very well.
canonCard.viewport: A search-led header, category chips, and rows of model cards with price and download badges.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other model repository by design.
